findings.element: Use a custom rule for this integration master switch (#c-engine) — and therefore the whole overlay body
findings.finding: On a fresh keyboard-only open the overlay holds exactly three focusable elements — close, Cancel and Save — because the master switch cannot take focus at all, so sections 1 to 3 are never rendered and there is nothing to configure.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user can open the configurator and then do nothing inside it: the rule can never be switched on, so defining how Synder finds the invoice is impossible without a mouse.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the master switch a real focusable switch (button with role=switch and aria-checked, or a checkbox) that responds to Enter and Space, so the sections it gates can be reached.

evidence.action: Focused Configure and pressed Enter to open the overlay, then pressed Tab repeatedly from the close button; separately called .focus() on the master switch and pressed Enter and then Space.
evidence.observed: The tab sequence inside the overlay was close, Cancel, Save, then straight out into the page behind; querying the overlay for focusables returned only those three; .focus() on the switch left activeElement elsewhere, and after both Enter and Space the engine was still off with the scope rows absent from the DOM.

findings.element: Every select and number input in the overlay — source, comparison, days, and the three selects on each condition row
findings.finding: Each of these controls computes an empty accessible name because the visible labels are spans, not label-for elements, and on condition rows after the first the label span is rendered as an empty string so the row has no label even visually.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader user hears three unnamed comboboxes in a row and cannot tell which one reads the payment, which is the comparison and which reads the invoice, so the rule cannot be built or checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace every field-label span with a real label element bound to its control, and emit the labels on every condition row rather than only the first, visually hiding them after row one.

evidence.action: Added a second condition row, then read the Chromium accessibility tree over CDP for the scope selects, the days field and both condition rows.
evidence.observed: Every control returned an empty name — the second row source came back as combobox with name empty and value Payment metadata, and the days field as spinbutton with name empty and value 90 — and element.labels was 0 for the text inputs; the only names present anywhere came from placeholder text.

findings.element: The full-screen overlay, its close / Cancel / Save controls and the Escape handler
findings.finding: The overlay is a generic div with no dialog role, no aria-modal and no accessible name; focus is never moved into it on open, the page behind stays reachable, and all four close paths leave focus on body instead of returning it to the trigger.
findings.user_impact: Pressing Enter on Configure appears to do nothing — focus stays on the Configure button now hidden underneath the overlay, with nothing announced — and after closing, the user has lost their place and must tab from the top of the document.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the overlay role=dialog aria-modal=true with aria-labelledby pointing at the title, move focus to the close button on open, contain Tab within it while open, and restore focus to the trigger on every close path.

evidence.action: Focused Configure and pressed Enter, then closed the overlay four separate ways — Escape, Enter on Cancel, Enter on close, Enter on Save — reading activeElement after each, and pressed Tab forward from the last overlay control.
evidence.observed: After opening, activeElement was still the Configure button and elementFromPoint over its centre returned the overlay instead of the button; the overlay reported role generic with role, aria-modal and aria-label all null while the page behind carried neither inert nor aria-hidden; Tab from the last overlay control escaped to body and on into the breadcrumb links behind the overlay; and after every close activeElement was body.

findings.element: Blocking validation errors and the Save button, reached by pressing + Add condition
findings.finding: The blocking error is a plain div with no id, no alert role and no aria-live, it is not referenced by the field aria-describedby and the field carries no aria-invalid, while Save is set disabled and so drops out of the tab order entirely.
findings.user_impact: A user who adds a condition is silently blocked — nothing announces the error, the offending field is not flagged as invalid, and tabbing forward from Cancel leaves the dialog without ever meeting a Save button or learning why it disappeared.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each error an id referenced by the field aria-describedby with aria-invalid true, put the footer count in a role=alert live region, and keep Save focusable using aria-disabled instead of disabled.

evidence.action: Pressed Enter on + Add condition to add a second row — which defaults to Payment metadata and therefore needs a key — then inspected the error markup and pressed Tab forward from Cancel.
evidence.observed: The error div had role null, aria-live null and no id; the new key input had aria-describedby null, aria-invalid null and labels 0; the footer count message had role null and aria-live null; Save was disabled and Tab from Cancel went straight to body, skipping Save.

gaps: days-either-side field: the map records only a mouse commit; arrow-key stepping was never exercised. Exercised here — a single ArrowUp fires change, re-renders the overlay body and replaces the input node, so activeElement drops to body and two further ArrowUp presses leave the value stuck at 91. The field cannot be stepped by keyboard and stepping it once ejects focus from the dialog.

Escape mid-edit: the handler is bound on document with no guard, so typing into the metadata key and pressing Escape — the standard gesture for reverting a text field — closed the overlay and discarded everything. The same happens after using ArrowDown inside a select.

sample-payment cards: all four are divs with role, tabindex and aria-checked null, and Tab from the disclosure summary goes straight past them — so by keyboard only the pre-selected matched outcome can ever be evaluated, and the two worked examples that demonstrate what happens when nothing is found are unreachable.

invoice-date lock: the locked target field does expose its explanation as an accessible description, but the date row lock is an aria-hidden SVG whose title attribute is the only carrier of the restriction — and since the date toggle is not focusable, neither is ever reached. The adjacent hint paragraph carries the same explanation as real text, so the information is not lost, only the affordance is.
focus visibility checked and passing: close, Add condition, remove row, both ALL/ANY buttons, the three summaries and the selects all render a visible ring. No finding spent here.
